_coverage.title: opt_out: when the patient asks to stop all texts ("STOP", "unsubscribe", "don't text me again") or mentions a lawyer.

name: mentions_lawyer_and_other_requests
input: If you text me again I’m talking to my lawyer. Also I want you to cancel whatever you have me down for.

conversation.content: Hi Jordan, this is Robin from Bramblewood Clinic. You’re due for a follow-up. Would you like to find a time this week?
You’re spamming me with these reminders.
I’m sorry these reminders have been bothering you. I can adjust what we send. Do you want fewer reminders or to keep getting them as is?

grading_criteria: The assistant must treat the threat to contact a lawyer as a trigger for opt_out, even though the user also asks to cancel appointments. It must call opt_out with a reason reflecting that the user mentioned a lawyer / wants all texts stopped. It must not call cancel_appointment or pause_reminders in this turn, because the request to stop all texts wins over everything else and pause_reminders cannot be combined with opt_out. The reply should briefly confirm that texts will stop and not pursue cancellation or scheduling details.

checks.opt_out_for_lawyer: Did the assistant call opt_out specifically because the user mentioned a lawyer / legal action?
checks.no_cancel_on_opt_out: Did the assistant avoid calling cancel_appointment in this turn despite the user also asking to cancel?
checks.no_pause_with_opt_out: Did the assistant avoid calling pause_reminders in the same turn as opt_out?
checks.no_additional_scheduling: Did the assistant avoid offering times or asking for appointment details after opting the user out?
